Arene C /C0H Bond Functionalization Coupling with Cyclization of
Allenes
Rong Zeng, a Juntao Ye,b Chunling Fu, a and Shengming Ma a,b,*
a Laboratory of Molecular Recognition and Synthesis, Department of Chemistry, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang, Hangzhou
310027, People/C29s Republic of China
b State Key Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of
Sciences, 345 Lingling Lu, Shanghai 200032, People/C29s Republic of China
Fax : (
+ 86)-21-6260-9305; e-mail: masm@sioc.ac.cn
Received: May 9, 2013; Published online: July 12, 2013
Supporting information for this article is available on the WWW under http://dx.doi.org/10.1002/adsc.201300408.
Abstract: Under the catalysis of a rhodium ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(III)
complex, the cyclization of 2,3-allenols was most
probably initiated with the C /C0H bond functionaliza-
tion of N-methoxybenzamides using the tetrame-
thylcyclopentadiene anion (C 5Me4
/C0) as ligand, af-
fording differently substituted 2,5-dihydrofuran de-
rivatives. Highly efficient axial-to-central chirality
transfer has been observed.
Keywords: 2,3-allenols; C /C0H activation; 2,5-dihy-
drofurans; coupling–cyclization; rhodium catalysts
The transition metal-catalyzed C /C0H functionalization
of arenes has been extensively explored to form C /C0C
bond or C /C0X bond(s) via reactions such as arylation,
alkenylation, alkylation, halogenations (I, Br, Cl, F),
amination, oxygenation, etc. (Scheme 1).
[1–3] On the
other hand, transition metal-catalyzed cyclization re-
actions of allenes with a nucleophilic functionality in
the presence or absence of organic halides have been
proven to be a powerful and efficient tool for the con-
struction of cyclic compounds.
[4–5] We envisioned
a coupling–cyclization of functionalized allenes in-
volving the functionalization of a C /C0H bond in arenes
(Ar/C0H).
[3] The challenge is the matching of the reac-
tivity of the organometallic intermediates formed
from the C /C0H bond metalation with the cyclization of
allenes. Herein, we wish to report the realization of
such a concept: Rh ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(III)-catalyzed coupling–cycliza-
tion reactions of allenols with N-methoxybenzamides
with the oxygen in air as the oxidant,
[6,7] providing
2,5-dihydrofuran derivatives, which play important
roles in organic chemistry, not only as key structural

units in many natural products and pharmaceuticals
but also as useful building blocks in synthetic chemis-
try.
[8]
As a first try, the Rh-catalyzed coupling–cyclization
reaction of 1.0 equiv. of 5-cyclohexyl-2-methylpenta-
3,4-dien-2-ol 2a with 1.2 equiv. of N-methoxybenz-
ACHTUNGTRENNUNGamide 1a catalyzed by 2.5 mol% of [Cp*RhCl
2]2 with
30 mol% of CsOAc was conducted at room tempera-
ture in MeOH/H 2O (20/1). Gratifyingly, the reaction
did afford the expected coupling–cyclization product
3aa in 57% NMR yield (entry 1, T able 1), together
with a small amount of an unidentified product. Then
the solvent effect was explored: MeOH gave a lower
yield (54%) with no 2a being recovered (entry 2,
Table 1); toluene and t-BuOH only afforded 37% and
34% yields of product 3aa together with 12% and
38% recovery of allenol 2a, respectively (entries 3
and 5, Table 1); DMF led to the worst result: 14% of
3aa together with 88% recovery of 2a after stirring
for 40 h (entry 4, Table 1). Different inorganic acet-
ACHTUNGTRENNUNGates were then screened: LiOAc·2 H
2O gave the simi-
lar result yielding 3aa in 58 % yield (entry 6, Table 1),
while Cu ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(OAc)2,[5,6] which also could be an oxidant,
gave a lower yield (53%) (entry 7, T able 1); to our de-
light, the readily available and inexpensive NaOAc
gave a higher yield of 3aa (62%) (entry 8, Table 1);
EtCOONa led to a lower yield (46%) (entry 9,
Table 1). In the presence of NaOAc, the reactions cat-
alyzed by [Cp*IrCl
2]2 or [Cp*RuCl 2]2 proceeded with
a much higher recovery (entries 10 and 11, T able 1).
Furthermore, it is interesting to observe that RhCl 3
failed to afford any expected product (entry 2,
Table 2); [CpMe
4RhCl2]2 was then used to catalyze
the reaction with the purpose of reducing the steric
hindrance of the applied ligand, which may favor the
C/C0H bond functionalization and oxymetalation.
Luckily, the yield of 3aa was improved to 66%
(entry 3, T able 2), and could be further increased to
70% by adding 10 mol% of additional tetramethylcy-
clopentadiene (C
5H2Me4) (entry 4, Table 2). This
steric effect of the ligand was further confirmed by
using the more sterically hindered ligand tetraphenyl-
cyclopentadiene (C
5H2Ph4) with 50% yield of 3aa
(entry 5, T able 2). Increasing the amount of C 5H2Me4
to 20 mol% afforded a lower yield with a trace recov-
ery of 2a (entry 6, Table 2). Surprisingly, the yield
could be improved to 72% by decreasing the loading
of 1a to 1.0 equiv. (entry 7, Table 2). Thus, we defined
the coupling–cyclization reaction of allenols and
1.0 equiv. of N-methoxybenzamides in MeOH/H
2Oa t
25 8C in air in the presence of 2.5 mol% of
[CpMe4RhCl2]2, 10 mol% of C 5H2Me4, and 30 mol%
of NaOAc as the standard reaction conditions for fur-
ther investigation.
With the optimized conditions in hand, the scope of
the cyclization–coupling reactions was explored with

and the corresponding coupling–cyclization products
may be obtained in moderate yields. Using allenol 2b,
differently substituted N-methoxybenzamides 1 were
also applied: either electron-donating substituents
such as 4-OMe ( 1c), or electron-withdrawing groups,
such as 4-Br ( 1b), 4-COOMe ( 1h), 3-NO
2 (1d), 3-CF 3
(1e), and 2-Cl-4-Br groups ( 1f) are accommodated.
Finally, the reaction can be easily conducted on a 10-
mmol scale of the substrate 2b in a similar yield
(entry 14, Table 3). The structures of the compounds
were further conformed by the X-ray single crystal
diffraction study of 3ae (Figure 1).
[9]
In addition, when N-methoxy-1-naphthylformamide
1g was applied, the 2-position C /C0H bond reacted ex-
clusively to afford the corresponding product 3gb in
71 % yield [Eq. (1)], no reaction occurred at the 8-po-
sition C/C0H bond of the naphthyl ring.
[10]
Four possible pathways have been proposed for this
coupling–cyclization reaction as summarized in
Scheme 2: (i) C /C0H rhodation of 1a provides the inter-
mediate M1,
[3e,f,11] which is followed by the coordina-
tion of the allene moiety in 2b with Rh and cyclic
oxyrhodation to afford M2. Reductive elimination
would yield the product 3ab (path A, Scheme 2); (ii)
carbometallation of allenol 2b with M1 would afford
the p-allyl rhodium intermediate M3,[13–14] which
would yield 3ab by intramolecular nucleophilic substi-
tution with the hydroxy group (path B, Scheme 2);
(iii) cyclic oxyrhodation of 2b with Rh ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(III) would
afford the 2,5-dihydrofuryl rhodium intermediate M4,
which may be followed by aryl rhodation with 1a to
afford M2. Reductive elimination would yield 3ab
(path C, Scheme 2); (iv) protonolysis of M4 would
afford 4b, which would couple with 1a to afford M2
and subsequently 3ab (path D, Scheme 2).
T o further probe the reaction mechanism, firstly,
the KIE ( kH/kD) was determined to be 4:1 or 5:1, re-
spectively, by running the reaction shown in Eq. (2)
or Eq. (3), indicating that the C /C0H bond cleavage
process should be a crucial step.
Moreover, the cyclization of 2b was carried out
under the standard conditions in the absence of N-
methoxybenzamide 1a (upper reaction in Scheme 3).
Interestingly, the reaction only afforded 10% of cyclo-
isomerization product 4b together with 76% recovery
of 2b even after 25 h; the yield of 4b could be im-
proved to 88% only when 50 mol% of the catalyst
was used. These results indicated that the formation
of intermediate M4 in Scheme 2 was a rather slow
process in the reaction, indicating that at least path C
may not be the predominant pathway. It was also ob-
served that the reaction of the cycloisomerization
product 4b with 1a failed to afford the product 3ab,
excluding the possibility of path D (lower reaction in
Scheme 3).
Furthermore, the optically active allenols R-2b and
S-2b were synthesized
[12] and submitted to the reac-
tions with N-methoxybenzamides 1a–1c under the
standard conditions. Gratifyingly, the efficient axial-
to-central chirality transfer from R-2b and S-2b to the
corresponding optically active 2,5-dihydroduran deriv-
atives was observed (Table 4). These results may
mostly exclude the path B, in which the s-p-s rear-
rangement of p-allyl rhodium intermediate M3 would
lead to racemization.
[4,13–16] In conclusion, although we

In summary, we have developed a rhodium-cata-
lyzed coupling–cyclization reaction of allenols with N-
methoxybenzamides using the tetramethylcyclopenta-
dienyl group as ligand. Optically active 2,5-dihydro-
furans could be synthesized by using axially chiral 2,3-
allenols
[12] through an efficient axial-to-central chirali-
ty transfer process. Mechanistic experiments indicated
that the reaction most likely first involves C /C0H rho-
dation of arenes, which is followed by cyclic oxyrho-
dation of allenols and reductive elimination to afford
the final coupling–cyclization products. The in-situ
generated Rh(I) would be reoxidized to Rh ACHTUNGTRENNUNG(III) with
the O
2 in the air to finish the catalytic cycle. Further
studies in this area including a further mechanistic
study are being carried out in our laboratory.

Experimental Section
Typical Procedure, Synthesis of 3aa
To a dried Schlenk tube equipped with a T eflon-coated mag-
netic stirring bar were added 1a (151.0 mg, 1.0 mmol),
[(CpMe4)RhCl2]2 (15.0 mg, 0.025 mmol), NaOAc (25.5 mg,
0.3 mmol), tetramethylcyclopentadiene (13.8 mg, 85%
purity, 0.1 mmol)/MeOH (2 mL), 2a (178.9 mg, 1.0 mmol)/
MeOH (4 mL), and water (0.3 mL) sequentially at 25
8C.
After being stirred for 30 h, the reaction was complete as
monitored by TLC, filtration through a short pad of silica
gel (eluent: Et
2O) and evaporation afforded the crude prod-
uct, which was purified by flash column chromatography on
silica gel (eluent: 30–60 8C petroleum ether/ethyl acetate = 4/
1 to 3.5/1 to 3.2/1) to afford 3aa as a solid; yield: 215.8 mg
(66%); mp 150.7–151.9 8C (hexane/dichloromethane);
